title: RBACv2: SAML-aware backfill with delta-resolver, audit-fidelity checks, and staged cutover runbook
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal: Safely migrate customers from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 while preserving audit fidelity and SAML identity mappings. This ticket coordinates the SAML-aware backfill, the delta-resolver for dual-write drift, automated reconciliation checks, synthetic canary harness, and the staged cutover runbook including rollback and support playbooks.

Scope:
- Implement an idempotent backfill job that materializes v2 role bindings from v1 authoritative store and SAML assertions.
- Add a delta-resolver service that computes and applies only conflicting deltas when dual-write is enabled.
- Ensure audit logs remain stable: every backfill action must emit an audit event with provenance (backfill|resolver|user-change).
- Create verification tooling (audit-fidelity-checker) that validates 1:1 mapping between pre-migration and post-migration effective permissions for sampled principals.
- Provide SSO/SAML mapping tests and an operator-facing lookup endpoint to debug nameId / assertion attribute transforms.
- Staged cutover plan: shadow, synthetic canary, opt-in customers, broad dual-write, final cutover with admin override.

Design decisions and constraints: 
- Backfill must be throttled by tenant to avoid racking up DB write pressure and to preserve runtime SLOs. We will use token-bucket per-tenant with burst allowance and global concurrency cap.
- Dual-write approach: start with asynchronous dual-write + write-ahead log per request; after observing low drift run a short-lived synchronous-dualwrite mode for canary orgs before global switch.
- Delta-resolver will use a deterministic conflict ordering: user-initiated changes always win; otherwise v2 authoritative canonical wins. Resolver must be idempotent and record decisions in an audit table.
- Audit logs: every mutation (backfill/resolver/dual-write) emits structured JSON containing: actor, source (migration|dualwrite|user), affected_principal, roles_before, roles_after, request_id, timestamp. Keep these in append-only audit stream and surface in Console logs for first 30 days.

Acceptance criteria:
- Audit-fidelity-checker passes for 99% of sampled principals across 10 canary tenants.
- Delta drift after 48 hours of async dual-write < 0.1% (reconciliation target).
- No increase in p95 API latency > 25ms for authz checks during backfill windows.
- Operator runbook steps for rollback validated via simulator (see attachments).

Operational runbook highlights (short):
1) Start tenant-shadow: enable shadow write for tenant T, run backfill in dry-run mode emitting audit events but not applying v2.
2) Run audit-fidelity-checker and permission-diff report. If > 0.5% mismatch, pause and open ENG bug.
3) Enable async-dual-write with WAL for 1h. Monitor reconciliation drift and error rate.
4) Promote selected tenants to synchronous-dual-write for 24h. Run synthetic canaries (create, modify, revoke bindings).
5) If canaries pass and drift < 0.1%, schedule broad dual-write and gradual cutover with communications.
6) Final cutover: disable v1 read path after a 7-day stabilization window. Keep audit stream retention policy to 90 days for migration events.

Rollback/Failure modes:
- High drift during async-dual-write: switch to per-tenant write block and initiate full reconciliation for affected tenants.
- Spike in authz latency: throttle backfill throughput and increase per-tenant backoff.
- SAML mapping failures: flip tenant opt-out (admin flag) and surface human-readable SAML mapping diagnostics to support.

Customer comms summary:
- Pre-cutover announcement: 2 weeks prior email, include impact, scheduled windows, opt-out instructions.
- Canaries: invite 5 low-risk customers to early opt-in with rollback guarantee.
- Post-cutover: publish audit export procedure and where to find SAML mapping reports in Console.

Links to artifacts and refs: Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/r/rbacv2-migration-runbook, GH PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac/pull/4572 (delta-resolver), https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac/pull/4599 (backfill).

2025-01-12 - Spike complete for per-tenant throttling; determined token-bucket approach with global cap is feasible (notes in Confluence).

2025-01-16 - Audit-fidelity-checker prototype reports 98.1% parity on synthetic dataset; need to reduce edge-case mismatches around inherited group roles.
2025-01-18 - Design decision: user-initiated changes win on conflict. Documented in Confluence and updated resolver tests.
2025-01-20 - Ran synthetic canary suite against prod-like cluster. Observed p95 authz latency increase +18ms at peak backfill rate; lowered concurrency and re-ran. Latency now within targets.
2025-01-22 - Support playbook draft complete. Added admin opt-out flag and diagnostic endpoint for SAML nameId lookups. Owner: Priya Singh.
